_source.document: teslam.io Whitepaper — A Sustainable Drive-to-Earn Community Economy on OEM-Attested Telemetry
_source.visibility: internal review only — not published, not linked from this site
_source.why: data/model.json feeds every figure the site renders. This file records what the whitepaper actually says, so the two cannot drift apart silently. tests/whitepaper-parity.test.ts fails the build when they do. Update this file only when the whitepaper is revised, and bump `version` when you do — that makes the revision an explicit act rather than a quiet edit.
_source.tags: The whitepaper marks each figure 확정 (settled) / 검증 (externally checked) / 제안 (proposed here) / 가정 (assumed). The tag is carried through so a reader knows how much weight a number holds.

_verification.what_this_file_proves: That the site agrees with the whitepaper. It does NOT prove the whitepaper is right. Those are different claims and only the first one is enforced by a test.

evidence: Tesla developer documentation quotes Fleet Telemetry at roughly $0.00667 per vehicle-hour at roughly 1,000 signals per hour, which is 1/150,000 per signal.
The published GBP tariff of 195,058.52 signals per £1 converts to approximately 150,000 signals per $1 at prevailing rates.
signalsPerUsd.gap: developer.tesla.com/docs/fleet-api/billing-and-limits returned HTTP 403 to automated retrieval, so the primary page was not read directly. The whitepaper's own footnote requires re-confirmation in the developer console before contract — that step is still outstanding and cannot be done from here.

unmodelled_credit.finding: Tesla applies a $10 monthly credit per developer account, described as covering streaming plus 100 commands and two wakes per day for two vehicles.
unmodelled_credit.impact: The whitepaper models Genesis 500 at KRW 33,360/month (~$24) with no credit applied. A $10 credit is roughly 40% of that bill. The published figure therefore overstates the real cost.
unmodelled_credit.direction: Conservative — the site claims a higher cost than it would pay, which strengthens rather than weakens the argument that API fees are a rounding error. Left uncorrected here because the fixture must record what the whitepaper says, not what it should say. Raise it in the next whitepaper revision.

fxKrwPerUsd.drift: about 1.8% stale, in the direction of understating cost in won
fxKrwPerUsd.note: The whitepaper tags this 가정 and says to re-quote before any published cost claim. The site publishes it, so the re-quote is owed. Changing it moves every won figure on /model, so it is left to the operator rather than edited here.

signalsPerUsd.note: Fleet Telemetry metered tariff: $1 per 150,000 signals. This is the October 2024 revision, a 15× reduction from the original $0.0001/signal proposal. Re-confirm in the developer console before any published cost claim.

samplingIntervalSeconds.note: Base signal set S0 is received once per 60 seconds, while driving only. Nothing is received while parked.

signalCount.note: latitude, longitude, vehicle speed, odometer — the minimal set that proves a drive.
signalCount.basis: Two, not four. Tesla categorises Odometer as `Vehicle State` and VehicleSpeed as `Driving`; neither needs the vehicle_location scope, which was separated out of vehicle_device_data in late 2024. Latitude and longitude were in the list because the older API handed them over whether or not you wanted them. Asking for them now is a deliberate act, and this site has no reason to perform it — accrual is decided by the odometer alone. See docs/reference/tesla-fleet-api/.

dailyCapDrv.note: Daily ceiling, equivalent to 50 km of earning.

pegDrv.note: Display peg: 1,000 DRV ≈ KRW 500 of goods, so 1 DRV = KRW 0.5. A catalogue price, not a market price.

genesisSeats.note: The closed cohort that measures the redemption mix. §7.3 Figure 5 is the reason 500 exists.

genesisRewardMultiplier.note: Genesis cohort multiplier, applied after the daily cap so the cap cannot be bypassed by it.

tslmTotalSupply.note: Fixed supply. Not issued. Issuance is contingent on the legal analysis in §11.3.

partnerCommissionRate.note: κ, the partner commission recovered on redemption. No partner is contracted.

redemptionMix.note: (φc, φb, φs). The whitepaper calls this the single most important unvalidated number in the model. The site names the third share `stakedToTslm`; the whitepaper calls the same quantity 락업 / locked. Same 0.25, different word.

apiKrwPerVehicleMonth.note: 4 signals × 60/hr × 1 hr/day × 30 days ÷ 150,000 × 1,390. The whitepaper rounds to 67.

genesisApiKrwPerMonth.note: The whitepaper states Genesis 500 costs KRW 33,360/month in API fees in total.

apiShareOfCashCost.note: API is 3.2% of net cash cost under the base redemption mix. This is the whole argument of the /model page: the binding constraint is redemption, not telemetry.

documentStatus.why: Tesla categorises Odometer as `Vehicle State` and VehicleSpeed as `Driving`; neither requires the vehicle_location scope, which was separated out of vehicle_device_data in late 2024. The whitepaper's four-signal figure assumed the older behaviour, where latitude and longitude arrived whether you asked for them or not. Halving the signals halves the API cost.
documentStatus.action: Revise the whitepaper. Until that happens this fixture is a transcription of what the document should say, not of what it says — which is the one thing it is not supposed to be, and is why this block exists rather than a quiet edit.
